svg.title: AI-Powered Insurance Claims Assistant: architecture
svg.desc: A handler or administrator uses a React UI served by a FastAPI service. Eleven agents each run as a LangGraph node: seven in the investigation graph (classify, investigate, risk, recommend, validate, supervise, judge) and four in the retrieve sub-graph. The investigation graph, checkpointed in SQLite, runs classify, retrieve, investigate, risk, recommend, validate, supervise, judge and review. Retrieve is a sub-graph in which four agents (Policy Passage Retriever, Procedure Graph Navigator, Knowledge Q&A Agent, Claims History Analyst) run side by side and are joined; supervise is a sub-graph that may send a brief back once for repair; the judge runs in the background; review is a human interrupt. Each agent may call only the tools on its roster. The three Synapt agents read the synapt_capstone1 provider over MCP (handling procedures and its knowledge graph as documents, 2,000 settled past claims in its ticket store, promoted lessons), with a labelled local fallback after a real Synapt failure. The Claims History Analyst queries the 100-million-row claims dataset with DuckDB. The Risk Analyst uses scikit-learn models. Model agents call NVIDIA NIM (Nemotron writes, gpt-oss-20b judges). Spans, runs, audit, feedback, side questions and accounts are stored in SQLite. Promoted lessons are ingested into Synapt and a human's rating of a knowledge-base answer is sent to Synapt as feedback.
svg.text: Synapt knowledge base + 100M-row claims history · eleven agents, each a LangGraph node · human review gate
React UI (Vite build in static/, served by the same FastAPI app)
Investigation: claim-sentence intake, live agent team and call list, early preview, brief with evidence and knowledge graph, side chat, feedback · Saved cases · Explainability · Agents
Administrator only: Observability (traces, metrics) · Quality & models (evaluations, training) · Connection (Synapt status and stats) · Accounts
JSON over HTTP · session cookie + CSRF
sessions, CSRF, API key, user / admin roles
strict Pydantic schemas; PII masked for models
Intake extractor: a model reads the notes;
a value is kept only if quoted word for word
Side chat: routed answers from Synapt or
the saved run; never edits the brief
11 agent nodes: 7 here + 4 in the retrieve sub-graph · review is the human gate · checkpointed in SQLite
2 Retrieve · a sub-graph of its own (retrieval/graph.py)
four agents start together; Synapt agents may add one model-guided search
assemble_evidence → passages · procedures · the claim · past cases · lessons
handler summary; at most one repair (redoes 3–6)
Every finding and recommendation cites a supplied source.
Agents hold only their roster tools, checked on every call; none can write to Synapt.
Nothing here approves, denies or pays a claim; the handler decides.
ticket store: 2,000 settled past claims (similar claims)
reads: get_chunks, search, get_procedures, traverse, query, tickets
Parquet file, authoritative for every number shown
sorted native copy for the 300-candidate search
cohort summary tables for exact settled figures
Anthropic Claude available as a provider setting
spans for every stage, tool and model call;
investigations, audit, feedback, spans, api_requests, side_questions, query_feedback
users and sessions · LangGraph checkpoints on a separate connection
golden cases and DeepEval; judge verdicts
shown on the Quality & models page
Feedback loops (a person decides each step)
Lessons: handler accepts and rates a brief → administrator promotes the reviewed lesson (no claim identifiers) → ingested into Synapt (trident_ingest)
→ retrieved as cited handler_lesson evidence in later investigations of the same claim type. Nothing is promoted automatically; a lesson never decides a claim.
Answers: the handler rates the knowledge base's answer as helpful, partly helpful or not → sent to Synapt as trident_feedback (no agent can send feedback).
